summary: Integrate Web Worker-based v86 WebAssembly Alpine Linux VM
description: Implement a standalone Web Worker wrapper to boot a minimal WebAssembly Alpine Linux image. This offloads x86 instruction execution from the browser's UI thread.
acceptance_criteria: Worker compiles and boots Alpine in under 3 seconds
No dropped frames on main window dragging
Successfully pipes Serial Out streams

summary: Implement Transactional Sync and Auto-Save for JSONL.gz Storage
description: Create an auto-save loop in CompressedStorageEngine that tracks file state dirty bits. If a file is modified, perform a debounced transactional append into IndexedDB.
acceptance_criteria: Changes auto-saved after 500ms of user/app idle
IndexedDB transaction commits raw binary ArrayBuffer
Decompression retrieves 100% of data with zero corruption

summary: Establish Reverse Proxy Engine for Installing Third-Party CORS-Protected Plugins
description: Create a CORS bypass engine using a secure pre-configured proxy helper to pull external manifest files from non-CORS domains.
acceptance_criteria: Fetch metadata from external links
Apply strict input sanitization on manifest JSON attributes
Reject non-secure origins

summary: Implement Event Hook Interceptors and Multi-Agent Orchestrator
description: Design system-level hooks inside the OS kernel to allow a background Agent to listen to user operations and coordinate sub-agents using capability tokens.
acceptance_criteria: Global event bus exposes system triggers safely to Agent
Orchestrator Agent can securely request fs:write
Automatic compilation of reports in VFS without human intervention

summary: Implement KB-MCP Integration for Browser-Based AI Agent
description: Integrate Vortex OS with the centralized KB-MCP server to provide persistent long-term semantic, episodic, and procedural memory to the in-browser AI Agent. Implement secure Host-side capability token verification ('kb-mcp:read', 'kb-mcp:write') before forwarding REST requests to https://kb.yapweijun1996.com.
acceptance_criteria: Sandboxed plugin cannot access KB-MCP server without declaring 'kb-mcp:read' or 'kb-mcp:write' permissions
Host OS successfully routes valid, tokenized messages over the MessageChannel IPC
AI Agent successfully reads/writes vector items through the CORS-authorized Host proxy

summary: Resolve Terminal Iframe Direct Load and Missing Worker Assets
description: Resolve the blank screen/script execution error caused by loading raw v86-bridge.js inside the Terminal iframe. Create a proper terminal.html plugin using a terminal emulator UI like xterm.js, and provide placeholder assets.
acceptance_criteria: Terminal icon loads terminal.html rather than raw script
terminal.html properly instantiates the MessageChannel
Loading of Web Worker does not fail with 404

summary: Implement VFS Concurrent Write Mutex Lock
description: Prevent data collisions and file corruption by designing an asynchronous transactional Mutex (Mutual Exclusion) lock mechanism inside jsonl-storage-engine.js.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent writes to the same filePath are queued sequentially
The queue resolves in order without throwing transactional abort errors
Gzip file retains 100% data integrity under concurrent write stresses

summary: Implement CORS Proxy Bypass for Third-Party Manifest Fetching
description: Introduce a configurable CORS bypass proxy helper in index.html to allow downloading plugin manifests from remote non-CORS enabled servers.
acceptance_criteria: Dynamic App installation fetches manifests from third-party domains without triggering CORS block
The proxy path is configurable from the settings panel
Robust sanitization applies to proxy response before parsing

summary: Fix Manifest Permission Token Grammar for KB-MCP Capabilities
description: Chrome DevTools review on 2026-05-20 found that installing the bundled local manifest.json fails because plugin-installer.js rejects kb-mcp:read. The permission tokenizer currently does not allow hyphenated capability namespaces before the first colon.
acceptance_criteria: Installing http://localhost:5173/manifest.json from the Add App modal succeeds
kb-mcp:read and kb-mcp:write are accepted as valid permission tokens
Malformed or unsafe permission strings are still rejected
Regression coverage proves the bundled manifest can pass sanitization

summary: Add User-Facing KB-MCP Configuration and Health Check
description: KB-MCP runtime setup previously required window.vortexKernel.configureKb({ apiKey, kbId }) from the browser console. Settings now saves KB ID and API key presence, hides the raw saved key on reopen, and exposes a Check KB status action.
acceptance_criteria: Settings can save KB ID and API key presence without rendering the raw saved key
A health check reports configured, missing-key, missing-KB, and request-failed states clearly
A sandboxed plugin can complete a kb:read request through the host proxy after configuration
Unauthorized plugins continue to receive capability-denied errors
verification: Chrome DevTools MCP confirmed saved key is hidden after reopening Settings
Chrome DevTools MCP confirmed missing and configured Settings states render clearly
Live KB success requires valid user-provided credentials

summary: Wire or Disable Placeholder Dock Apps
description: Dashboard, Files, and Terminal Dock icons now open functional windows. Repeated Dock clicks focus or restore an existing system window instead of spawning duplicates.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard and Files either open functional windows or render as visibly unavailable
Clicking every enabled Dock icon produces an observable result
The behavior is covered by a browser smoke check
verification: Chrome DevTools MCP confirmed Dashboard Dock clicks keep one window and restore minimized windows

summary: Add Favicon Asset to Remove Browser 404 Noise
description: The main route now links a small SVG favicon so browser reviews no longer confuse missing favicon noise with runtime failures.
acceptance_criteria: Loading http://localhost:5173/ no longer produces a favicon 404
Console and network reviews can distinguish real runtime issues from asset noise

summary: Fix WebContainer npm Global Install Prefix
description: Vortex OS Terminal previously let npm global installs target /usr/local/lib/node_modules inside WebContainer, causing EACCES for commands such as npm i -g @openai/codex. Global npm commands now use /home/.npm-global unless the user provides an explicit prefix.
acceptance_criteria: Global npm installs in Terminal use a writable WebContainer prefix
npm config get prefix reports /home/.npm-global
User-provided --prefix arguments are respected
verification: Chrome DevTools MCP confirmed npm config get prefix returns /home/.npm-global
Chrome DevTools MCP confirmed npm i -g @openai/codex normalizes to include --prefix /home/.npm-global

description: Terminal now loads Pyodide from the CDN module at runtime instead of statically bundling the pyodide package, removing Vite externalization warnings while preserving on-demand Python support.
acceptance_criteria: Terminal still boots Pyodide on demand
Production build completes without Pyodide externalization warnings
verification: npm run build completed successfully with no Pyodide externalization warnings

summary: Execute npm Global Binaries from Terminal Shell
description: After npm i -g @openai/codex succeeded in WebContainer, typing codex still returned codex: command not found because Vortex shell only dispatched built-in commands and did not route installed global npm binaries. Unknown safe command names now try /home/.npm-global/bin/<command> and then WebContainer PATH lookup after WebContainer has booted.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown safe command names are checked against WebContainer global npm binary paths after WebContainer has booted
Installed npm global binaries can be executed directly from Vortex shell
Non-installed commands still return a shell-level command not found
verification: Chrome DevTools MCP confirmed npm i -g cowsay followed by cowsay hello renders cowsay output and does not print command not found
Chrome DevTools MCP confirmed npm i -g @openai/codex followed by codex --version executes the installed binary and does not print codex: command not found
